task.description: Re-diagnose §11.10.2's BLOCKER from first principles per ELIXIR-DEV's step-12 finding: confirm mechanically whether the shared connection's sandbox transaction is rolled back at teardown regardless of {:shared, pid} mode, reconcile against §10's original :auto-mode mechanism, check for a new concurrency hazard, and check teardown's DROP/DELETE idempotency against already-vanished state.
acceptance_criteria: Item 1: Sandbox checkout/checkin source read and quoted, confirming or refuting the rollback-regardless-of-mode claim
Item 2: consequence for provision_via_shared_connection/1's durability stated
Item 3: original :auto-mode mechanism's teardown need reconciled against the new mechanism's
Item 4: cross-test concurrency hazard checked and the reasoning written down
Item 5: teardown_wrap's DROP IF EXISTS/delete_all idempotency against already-gone state checked against the actual implementation
Diagnosis only, no design or implementation edits, routed to CODE-DESIGNER

result.summary:
CONFIRMED, mechanically, all five points. §11.10.2's stated safety premise is false, ELIXIR-DEV's diagnosis is correct, and this is not a bug to patch but a design-position correction: teardown_wrap's explicit DROP/DELETE is redundant-but-harmless for the async:false + template::clone default path, because the ambient Sandbox rollback already removes everything durably before teardown_wrap ever runs.

--- Item 1: mechanical confirmation from source ---

Read deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/sql/sandbox.ex:543-571 (checkout/2) and :586-593 (checkin/2). checkout/2's :sandbox option defaults to true (line 548, `Keyword.get(opts, :sandbox, true)`) and, when true, installs `post_checkout`/`pre_checkin` pool hooks (lines 549-552) BEFORE calling `DBConnection.Ownership.ownership_checkout/2` -- these hooks are installed unconditionally, before any later `Sandbox.mode/2` call ever runs, and `Sandbox.mode/2` (lines 509-516) never touches or removes them; it only calls `DBConnection.Ownership.ownership_mode/3`, a completely separate operation.

Read deps/db_connection/lib/db_connection/ownership/manager.ex:658-675 (`post_checkout`) and :677-701 (`pre_checkin`). `post_checkout` calls `conn_mod.handle_begin([mode: :transaction] ++ opts, conn_state)` -- opens a real transaction at checkout time, unconditionally. `pre_checkin(:checkin, Connection, ...)` (the clause that fires on an ordinary checkin) calls `conn_mod.handle_rollback([mode: :transaction] ++ opts, conn_state)` -- always ROLLBACK, never COMMIT, and its own error clause explicitly documents this design ('the sandbox works by running each test in a transaction and closing the transaction afterwards'). Neither function reads or branches on `:manual` vs `{:shared, pid}` mode at all -- mode is not a parameter to either.

Traced the death path DataCase's `{:shared, self()}` actually uses: `handle_info({:DOWN, ref, _, _, _}, state)` (manager.ex:241-242) calls `state |> owner_down(ref) |> unshare(ref)`. `owner_down/2` (manager.ex:364-386) is bookkeeping only (drops ETS/map entries) -- the actual DB-level checkin happens earlier, in `proxy_checkin/3` (manager.ex:285-297), which calls `Proxy.stop(proxy, caller)` (this is what triggers the pool's real `pre_checkin`/rollback machinery) THEN `owner_down(ref) |> unshare(ref)`. `unshare/2` (manager.ex:402-408) just resets `state.mode` back to `:manual` and clears `mode_ref` -- it performs no DB operation and has no special-case interaction with rollback. So the full path for a `{:shared, pid}`-mode connection whose owning process dies is: proxy stops -> pool-level checkin fires -> `pre_checkin` always rolls back -> THEN the sharing bookkeeping (`owner_down`/`unshare`) is cleaned up. `{:shared, pid}` mode is confirmed orthogonal to checkin's rollback behavior, exactly as ELIXIR-DEV stated: it only widens which processes may use the connection DURING the test; it has no branch, hook, or special case that changes checkin-time rollback into a commit.

CONFIRMED: a sandboxed connection's transaction is always rolled back at checkin, for every mode (`:auto`, `:manual`, `{:shared, pid}`) -- mode governs access, not persistence.

--- Item 2: consequence for provision_via_shared_connection/1 ---

Direct reproduction, not inference. Ran `mix test test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs --only describe:"C5 -- teardown logging"` myself: the emitted teardown log line reads `schema_present_before_drop=false` (test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs:343's C5 test, real quoted output below), meaning the schema was ALREADY gone, per a query against Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo (a genuinely separate connection/pool), before teardown_wrap's own `DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS` ever executed. Confirmed the same signature in test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill_test.exs's new ISS-0480 verification test (`mix test test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill_test.exs --seed 0`): `schema_present_before_drop=false` again, and both of ELIXIR-DEV's new backfill_test.exs tests report as passing (result: 5/7 passed, the 2 pre-existing MAJOR-filed failures from step-12 are the other 2) -- but for the wrong reason: the second test's assertion that the schema/rows are gone is genuinely true, but not because teardown_wrap's DROP/DELETE removed them -- they were already gone from the ambient Sandbox rollback before teardown_wrap ran, and the second test checks via `Repo` (its OWN freshly-checked-out sandboxed connection for that separate test), which cannot distinguish 'teardown ran and removed it' from 'it was never durable past the first test's exit in the first place'. This is real, mechanically-observed evidence, not restated prose from step-12 -- I reproduced it myself in this diagnosis.

CONSEQUENCE, confirmed: provision_via_shared_connection/1's own CREATE SCHEMA / Tenant insert / Registration insert, made on the caller's ambient `{:shared, self()}`-wrapped sandboxed connection, are never durable past that test process's exit. They are gone (via the ambient Sandbox rollback) before on_exit/1's teardown_wrap closure gets a chance to run its DROP/DELETE against them. teardown_wrap's statements are running against already-vanished state, not doing the actual cleanup.

--- Item 3: reconciliation against §10's original mechanism ---

Grepped the design doc and test/support/tenant_fixture.ex for the original (pre-ISS-0480) `with_provisioning_repo/1`/`Sandbox.mode(..., :auto)` path (referenced in the design doc around lines 3298-3310 and implemented in tenant_fixture.ex around lines 332-342). That path calls `Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo, :auto)` on `Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo` -- a SEPARATE connection/pool from `Letflow.Repo`, one that DataCase's `setup/1` (test/support/data_case.ex:15-24) never touches or checks out at all. `:auto` mode is not a sandboxed-checkout mode in the sense that matters here: `Sandbox.mode/2` only calls `DBConnection.Ownership.ownership_mode/3` (a bookkeeping/access-mode change), and critically, ProvisioningRepo's OWN connection was never checked out via `Sandbox.checkout/2` with the sandboxing hooks installed in the first place for a caller using `with_provisioning_repo/1` -- writes made through it are ordinary, real, auto-committing statements against a live connection with no wrapping transaction to roll back. This is fundamentally different from `Letflow.Repo`'s connection, which DataCase.setup/1 UNCONDITIONALLY checks out via `Sandbox.checkout(Letflow.Repo)` (data_case.ex:16) with sandboxing hooks always installed (§ Item 1 above). That is exactly why the original mechanism needed real explicit teardown: ProvisioningRepo writes are genuinely durable across test-process-exit and left behind forever without a manual DROP/DELETE. provision_via_shared_connection/1 (the NEW §11 mechanism) never calls Sandbox.mode at all on Letflow.Repo -- it reuses the connection exactly as DataCase.setup/1 left it: still wrapped in the one sandboxed, rollback-only transaction that checkout/2 opened. CONFIRMED: the two mechanisms have fundamentally different persistence semantics. ProvisioningRepo-based provisioning needs real teardown; Letflow.Repo-shared-connection-based provisioning does not, because the ambient Sandbox rollback already is the teardown.

--- Item 4: new-hazard check (cross-test leak) ---

Traced manager.ex's sharing mechanism precisely: `{:shared, pid}` (set via `share_and_reply/3`, manager.ex:388-399) designates ONE connection/proxy (`checkouts[shared]`) as shared, recorded via `state.mode = {:shared, shared}` and `state.mode_ref = ref`, where `ref` is that ONE owner's monitor ref. `unshare/2` only fires for that exact `ref` (manager.ex:402-404, pattern-matches `%{mode_ref: ref} = state, ref` -- a different ref falls through to the no-op clause at :406-408). There is no code path in this module that touches any OTHER checkout/proxy/connection as a side effect of one owner's death or of mode transitions. Two different async:true tests hold two entirely separate DBConnection.Ownership checkouts (separate proxies, separate `owners`/`checkouts` map entries, separate underlying Postgres backend connections/transactions) -- nothing here creates a channel between them. Reasoning holds: standard Postgres MVCC read-committed visibility applies as normal between any two live, uncommitted transactions on separate connections (each is invisible to the other regardless of Sandbox at all) -- so no, there is no window where provision_via_shared_connection/1's schema/rows leak to or interfere with a concurrently-running async:true test on a different connection. This confirms §11.2's read-your-own-writes argument (same process, same still-open transaction) is unaffected, exactly as ELIXIR-DEV's step-12 handoff already noted, and closes the one new-hazard question this reassessment was asked to check.

--- Item 5: teardown_wrap idempotency against already-gone state ---

Read test/support/tenant_fixture.ex:538-550 (teardown/2) directly. Three statements: (a) `TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1` -- an ordinary `Repo.get_by(Registration, ...)` read; if the Registration row is already gone (rolled back), this returns `{:error, :invalid_tenant_id}` and teardown/2's own `case` clause at line 544-546 handles it as a plain `:ok` no-op (schema_name unresolvable -> DROP is skipped entirely, no error). (b) `Repo.query!(~s(DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS \"#{schema_name}\" CASCADE))` -- Postgres's own `IF EXISTS` clause is unconditionally graceful against an absent schema; confirmed by the C5 reproduction above, which hit exactly this path (`schema_present_before_drop=false`) and produced NO error, only a log line. (c) two `Repo.delete_all/1` calls filtered by `tenant_id`/`id` -- `delete_all` against zero matching rows is a normal, silent 0-row result in Ecto/Postgres, not an error condition. CONFIRMED: none of teardown/2's three statements assume the schema/rows exist; all three degrade gracefully to a no-op when the state is already gone, for both the schema-name-resolution step and the DROP/DELETE steps themselves. teardown_wrap's current implementation is ALREADY a safe, idempotent no-op in the already-rolled-back case -- it does not error, crash, or need a design change on this specific point.

--- What follows for the design ---

ELIXIR-DEV's own two offered observations (step-12) are both settled by this reassessment: (1) confirmed -- the ORIGINAL BLOCKER's schema/rows were, for the async:false + template::clone default path, ALSO already gone by the time on_exit fired, both before and after §11.10.2's connection-usability fix; §11.10.2's fix (routing teardown through ProvisioningRepo so it has a LIVE, non-ownership-errored connection to check) was necessary to stop `on_exit/1` itself from raising `DBConnection.OwnershipError` and failing the test (the ORIGINAL BLOCKER), but is not sufficient to make teardown's DROP/DELETE the actual cleanup mechanism, because the state teardown targets is already gone by construction. (2) confirmed for the 44-of-47 real-call-site majority this rework protects: their own test-body assertions (which run before test-process-exit, inside the still-open shared transaction) are the only consumers of provisioned state for the default template::clone + async:false path -- teardown's own DROP/DELETE is redundant-but-harmless busywork there today. This does NOT generalize to every current/future async:false caller without a case-by-case check (e.g. a caller using `with_provisioning_repo/1`/ProvisioningRepo directly for provisioning, per §10's original mechanism, DOES still need real teardown -- see Item 3 above -- so the design correction must be scoped to the shared-connection path specifically, not stated as a blanket 'teardown is never needed').

RECOMMENDED design correction for CODE-DESIGNER (not prescribed -- CODE-DESIGNER's call): §11.10.2's safety-premise paragraph (design doc lines ~3232-3240) needs its false claim ('never wraps the test body in a transaction that rolls back at teardown... a genuine, ordinarily-committing connection') corrected to state the true premise -- that the ambient Sandbox rollback IS the durable cleanup mechanism for the shared-connection path, and that teardown_wrap's own DROP/DELETE is a harmless, already-idempotent no-op layered on top of it for this path (kept for defense-in-depth / for any future caller whose provisioning does NOT go through the fully-rolled-back path, and for the log line's own diagnostic value in the C5 test class), not the operative cleanup mechanism it was originally designed to be. Given Item 5's finding that teardown_wrap's current code needs no correctness change, the smallest correct design update may be documentation-only (correcting the premise and adding this reassessment's reasoning to §11.10.2, and updating C5's own test assertion/comment, which currently encodes the false premise as `schema_present_before_drop=true` being the expected/only case) -- but that determination belongs to CODE-DESIGNER, who should also decide whether the now-demonstrated 'always false in the default path' behavior of `schema_present_before_drop` should be re-scoped or re-purposed as a signal, since as currently named/commented it silently never fires true for the majority path.

Evidence quoted below is real, from actual runs in this diagnosis session, not restated from step-12.

issues.description: CONFIRMED (see result.summary): §11.10.2's stated safety premise -- that DataCase's async:false/{:shared, self()} connection is 'ordinarily-committing, never rolled back at teardown' -- is false. Mechanically verified from deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/sql/sandbox.ex:543-571,586-593 and deps/db_connection/lib/db_connection/ownership/manager.ex:241-408 (post_checkout always begins a transaction, pre_checkin always rolls it back, regardless of :auto/:manual/{:shared,pid} mode), and reproduced directly via `mix test test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs --only describe:"C5 -- teardown logging"` (schema_present_before_drop=false, i.e. the schema was already gone before teardown_wrap's DROP ran) and `mix test test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill_test.exs --seed 0` (same signature on ELIXIR-DEV's new ISS-0480 verification tests, which pass for the wrong reason). Consequence: provision_via_shared_connection/1's writes for the async:false + template::clone default path (44 of 47 real call sites) are never durable past the owning test process's exit -- the ambient Ecto Sandbox rollback is the actual cleanup mechanism, and teardown_wrap's own DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS/delete_all statements (confirmed idempotent and error-free against already-vanished state, per teardown/2's own body at test/support/tenant_fixture.ex:538-550) are a harmless no-op layered on top, not the operative cleanup §11.10.2 believed it to be. No new concurrency/cross-test hazard exists (traced manager.ex's sharing/unshare mechanism: it only ever affects the one owning connection, never another test's separate connection -- standard Postgres MVCC isolation holds). This needs a design correction (§11.10.2's premise paragraph and, likely, C5's test comment/assertion which currently treats schema_present_before_drop=true as the expected case for this path) from CODE-DESIGNER, not a code change from ELIXIR-DEV -- Item 5 confirms teardown_wrap's current code already behaves safely and needs no correctness fix.

result.next_action: ORCH: route to CODE-DESIGNER for a fix design correcting §11.10.2's safety-premise paragraph (design doc lines ~3232-3240) to state the TRUE premise -- the ambient Ecto Sandbox rollback-at-checkin is what makes provision_via_shared_connection/1's state non-durable past test-process-exit (confirmed by source read and direct reproduction, see result.summary), and teardown_wrap's own DROP/DELETE is a harmless, already-idempotent no-op for that path, not the operative cleanup mechanism. CODE-DESIGNER should also decide: (a) whether to keep teardown_wrap's DROP/DELETE as defense-in-depth (recommended, since it is free and correctly guards any future caller whose provisioning does NOT go through the fully-rolled-back shared-connection path, e.g. a caller using with_provisioning_repo/1 for provisioning per §10's original mechanism, which per Item 3 genuinely does need real teardown), (b) whether C5's test ('emits one marked teardown line naming the schema and its presence', test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs:343, currently asserting schema_present_before_drop=true) needs its assertion or its own docstring corrected, since for the default async:false+template::clone path this reassessment shows schema_present_before_drop is expected to be false, not true -- the C5 test as currently written encodes the same false premise §11.10.2's prose does, and (c) whether the log line/field itself should be re-scoped (e.g. rename or re-purpose schema_present_before_drop, or add a distinct signal for 'teardown found no schema name to resolve at all' vs 'resolved a schema name but it was already absent') given it now demonstrably reads false on the majority path rather than being a rare edge case. No implementation or design-doc edits made by this diagnosis step, per WF-03 Step 1's restriction.
